findings.name: hairline (lucasmarkes/hairline)
findings.what_it_does: MIT library of 33 pointer-reactive isometric line-drawn SVG figures for React or any DOM; no runtime dependencies, one shared animation loop. Ships agent skills hairline-create (draws a new figure as one HTML file) and hairline-adopt (rebuilds an SVG).
findings.how_we_use_it: v1: install exactly @lucasmarkes/hairline@0.5.1 (never unscoped 'hairline', an unrelated 2019 CSS package) or vendor 3-5 figures for empty canvas, onboarding, module cards. Skip the shadcn URL route in CI. Adopt its ten rules as our linework spec.
findings.last_activity: 2026-10-14 (v0.5.1; six releases from v0.1.0-rc.0 on 1 Oct)
findings.license: MIT (c) Lucas Marques; GitHub API and npm confirm MIT; monorepo package.json has no license field
findings.popularity: 2.57k stars, 157 forks, 5 open issues+PRs (21 Oct 2026); HN post 4 Oct: 2 points, 0 comments; 1 X post; 1 third-party article; 21st.dev listing; a second search for Reddit or LinkedIn reviews found nothing
findings.risks: Single maintainer; created 1 Oct, six releases since, so pin. GitHub description still says 'Six' figures (README: 33). Figures are generic, not architectural. shadcn route fetches from the author's own domain. Monorepo dev needs Node 22+.
findings.saves: Hours of hand-coded SVG animation.

findings.name: anatomy (wheresryan22/anatomy)
findings.what_it_does: MIT agent skill that builds an interactive isometric SVG figure (optional WebGL shaders, beta 3D) explaining an idea as a real machine. Ships a drawing kit, geometry audit, headless-Chrome checks and A4/Letter print sheets. Slow by design.
findings.how_we_use_it: Roadmap, test first: build one Figure (sun path or stack-effect shaft) and check it against our hairline-derived calm style before spending more tokens; drop it if the dense-machine look clashes on boards. Never ask for 'the tower'. Reuse its geometry-audit and loose-line checks as drawing QA.
findings.popularity: 18.0k stars, 1.4k forks, 61 open issues+PRs; created 8 Oct 2026; HN: 2 posts, 2 points, 0 comments; 4+ independent X, YouTube and Medium posts, enthusiastic but mostly descriptive
findings.risks: A whole building is Epic (6 h+, never started unasked). Even a Figure must be a dense 40-80 part machine, not slabs, which may clash with calm hairline style. CLI needs Node 22.20+; checks need Chrome. Print sheets are A4.
findings.saves: Design time only; Figure/Hero/Epic tiers help cap spend.

findings.name: text-to-cad (earthtojake/text-to-cad)
findings.what_it_does: MIT Claude Code plugin and skills letting agents generate STEP, GLB, STL, 3MF and DXF from text or images via build123d and Open CASCADE (cadgen), with viewer, drawings, DFM and printing skills. Mechanical focus: parts, robots, G-code.
findings.how_we_use_it: Roadmap: optional local experiment for odd-shaped massing or facade parts, GLB into our viewer. Not the v1 massing node: tower massing is extruded floor plates and it cannot write .3dm or IFC. Never bundle it in the browser app.
findings.popularity: 22.1k stars, 2.2k forks, 29 open issues+PRs; open-sourced 22 Apr 2026; HN thread 1 May: 186 points, 48 comments, mixed (about 5 of 17 commenters report supervised use, about 6 doubt spatial reasoning or the benchmarks)
findings.risks: Needs uv (not installed). Smart App Control blocks OCP unless off or under WSL; never turn it off (irreversible). Telemetry and daily update check default on: run uvx cadgen telemetry off once per machine; set CADGEN_UPDATE_CHECK=0.
findings.saves: Would avoid building a CAD kernel and viewer, but only for mechanical parts.

findings.name: Thermal-Sandbox-Web (GenEnv fork of christinachiu)
findings.what_it_does: Static app comparing annual solar load on a 215 x 130 m Winnipeg site (University of Manitoba), baseline vs scenario. Two JSON files drive it: Rhino-derived geometry and about 20k Ladybug/Radiance irradiance points. Three.js 0.160 viewer inside one 5 MB HTML file.
findings.how_we_use_it: v1, energy node only: precompute irradiance in Python (or user-side Ladybug), emit typed JSON, render in browser. Copy its meta-block idea (units, sources, notes, open-sky total, formulas); compare baseline and scenario point by point. Re-implement; copy no code.
findings.license: None (5-path tree has no LICENSE; API null; upstream also none)
findings.popularity: Fork: 1 star, 1 open PR; upstream: 0 stars, 1 fork
findings.risks: Permission must come from the upstream owner (licences: recommendation 2); author's affiliation unknown. Fork is 3 weeks behind. Winnipeg data, not Vancouver. Ladybug, the generating tool, is AGPL-3.0.
findings.saves: Output-schema and unit conventions (kWh/m2/yr; solar reduction = 1 - load / open-sky total) for the energy module.

findings.name: suncalc (mourner/suncalc)
findings.what_it_does: Tiny dependency-free JavaScript library (v2.1.1) for sun position, sunlight phases and moon data, based on Meeus formulas. Altitude is refraction-corrected, azimuth is degrees clockwise from north. BSD-2-Clause.
findings.how_we_use_it: Core: browser sun vectors for three.js shadow views and the PDT time slider. Build 10:00 PDT as 17:00 UTC, never from the viewer's time zone. Unit-test against our own NOAA-style Python calculation at 10:00, 13:00 and 16:00 PDT on 22 Sep (not run yet). Pin 2.1.1.
findings.risks: Single maintainer. Position only: no shadows or irradiance. It takes a UTC instant, so careless time-zone handling shifts the equinox window by hours. Tests need tolerances against other methods. Older tutorials may use other angle conventions.
findings.saves: Avoids writing sun-position astronomy in JavaScript.

Open the PDF in a browser first (403 to our tools); never encode park lists or thresholds from secondary sources.
findings.last_activity: Approved by Council 17 Sep 2025 (Daily Hive, dtmass README, search snippet of the PDF front matter); later amendments not checked
findings.license: City publication; reuse terms not checked

principles.principle: Hairline rule 'hit': pointer tests run against the resting pose, so hover never flickers.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Canvas nodes, ports and wires use static hit areas, not animated geometry, so hover and drag stay stable.

principles.principle: Hairline rules 'accent' and 'quiet': the stroke is the only highlight; no fills, glows or words inside the figure.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Keep a small calm palette and reserve one signal colour for FALSE ASSUMPTION so it never loses meaning; no decorative glow or badge noise.

principles.principle: Hairline rule 'rest': the resting state is composed with one bright mark showing where to look.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Every screen has one focal point and one next action (for example 'run module'), which keeps users focused without nudging tricks.

principles.principle: Hairline rules 'cost' and 'clock': animate only when needed, pause offscreen, long ease-out for discrete choices, springs for continuous tracking; reduced-motion lands instantly.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Set a motion budget: one shared animation loop, pause when hidden, honour prefers-reduced-motion, skip redraws when values are unchanged (matters for large canvases).

principles.principle: Anatomy: 'the object is the explanation'; displayed numbers come from a running model and must be true.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Every number on screen comes from a module's computed output and cites its source or is flagged a team assumption; no placeholder or invented figures.

principles.principle: Anatomy verifies visuals mechanically: geometry audit, zero loose line ends, headless screenshots at desktop and 390 px, close-ups.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Add automated visual QA (Playwright screenshots at desktop and phone width, overlap/clearance audit) before a module or board ships; cheaper in tokens than visual re-prompting.

principles.principle: Anatomy sizes work in tiers (Figure 40-80 parts, often under an hour; Hero 2-4 h; Epic 6 h+, never started unasked; a whole building is Epic) and demands dense many-part machines, never a few slabs.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Give AI-built visuals a size tier and time/token budget; ask before anything above the default tier; never request a whole-tower figure; test one figure against our calm hairline-derived style before committing to more.

principles.principle: Arch540 C_design_space: a provided evaluator is the only trusted source of numbers and is never edited by the agent. Its sun objective belongs to a teaching harness (80 x 60 m housing lot, at most 14 storeys, winter solstice, 9:00-15:00 solar time), not to a Vancouver regulatory test.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Each evaluation module is deterministic code with typed JSON outputs; the LLM orchestrates and explains but never invents metrics. The regulatory sun test is the City's equinox 10:00-16:00 PDT shadow test; the demo's solstice sun hours stay a secondary metric labelled 'course teaching metric'.

principles.principle: Arch540 B_testfit: a PreToolUse hook refuses failing output, at most six revisions, then stop and end with UNRESOLVED; never claim success without a passing check. A hook that cannot start is a non-blocking error unless onFailure is 'block' (Claude Code v2.1.295+), and onFailure has no effect on Stop-type hooks (A_writing's guard is one).
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Add an UNRESOLVED state and an iteration cap to every AI-assisted module run; gate outputs on a passing check, not the model's claim. Enforcing gates are PreToolUse hooks in exec form (venv python.exe, onFailure block); Stop-hook guards are advisory; a CI test checks hooks exit 0 or 2 on Windows.

principles.principle: rhino-gh-mcp gates AI access with scenario modes: Inspect, Tune, Coach (default), Execute, Author.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Give each node and the whole canvas an AI permission level, defaulting to read/suggest, so users stay in control and edits are traceable.

principles.principle: text-to-cad layering: skills are the product, shared core has no UI imports, apps never import apps, heavy kernel stays out of the server process, one pinned command per skill.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Structure our repo as core (graph and module contracts), ui, and apps, with heavy geometry/solar code in separate workers and pinned, reproducible commands for every module.

principles.principle: anatomy-community submits source, not built output; CI rebuilds in a locked sandbox with a two-run determinism check, previews, human review, per-item licence.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Community modules are uploaded as source plus manifest, rebuilt deterministically in a sandbox, previewed, reviewed, and carry a licence and source-citation field.

principles.principle: sala-tech-knowledge-tree keeps content as JSON with a validator for IDs and prerequisite cycles on every pull request, plus a verified-status field.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Module manifests are schema-validated in CI (unique IDs, no dependency cycles, required sources); status fields show verified, team assumption or FALSE ASSUMPTION.

principles.principle: Massing Studio and skills-for-architects mark code and zoning output as a draft for professional review and cite clauses.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Every compliance result shows clause citation, edition date and a 'draft, not a compliance determination' label.

principles.principle: Thermal-Sandbox-Web ships its data with a meta block (units, sources, notes, open-sky total, derived formulas) and compares baseline with scenario point by point.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Every module output carries a meta block (units, source citations, data version, derived formula, team-assumption flag) and supports baseline-vs-scenario comparison on identical points.

recommendations.decision: Core (by 13 Nov): adopt the Arch540 agents_demo pattern as our module contract, re-implemented for Windows: deterministic Python evaluator (numpy, scipy, shapely), JSON in/out, Pareto front, a gate that blocks failing output, UNRESOLVED after six revisions. Enforcing gates are PreToolUse hooks in exec form: command ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.venv/Scripts/python.exe, args [hook path], onFailure block (Claude Code v2.1.295+). Never python3, never .cmd shims. Stop-hook guards (A_writing style) are advisory. Portable file lock instead of fcntl; a CI test fails if any hook exits with anything but 0 or 2. If anyone runs Xun's demos as shipped, use WSL.
recommendations.rationale: Verified 21 Oct: A's guard is a Stop hook; B, C and D use PreToolUse; all call python3, C's evaluator imports fcntl, and python3 here is the Store alias (exit 49), so a gate would silently skip. Docs: onFailure has no effect on Stop, SubagentStop, TaskCompleted or TeammateIdle; exit 2 on a Stop hook still keeps Claude working when the hook runs, but a Stop hook that cannot start fails open. Exec form on Windows needs a real .exe; the venv path should qualify but is untested here.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Running the demos as-is on Windows; relying on onFailure for Stop-hook guards; LLM-computed metrics (hallucination and token cost); copying files before a licence; copying demo thresholds as Vancouver values (teaching values).

recommendations.decision: Core: the v1 primary sun/shadow node is the City's test. For each listed public park, plaza and school site, compute new shadow caused by the proposal (existing context subtracted) on 22 Sep, 10:00-16:00 PDT (UTC-7 clock time), cited to the Solar Access Guidelines for the Downtown Peninsula (Council 17 Sep 2025) and labelled draft, not a compliance determination. suncalc gives browser sun vectors; Python shapely projects floor-plate prisms per time step. Secondary, labelled 'course teaching metric': Arch540 solstice sun hours (9:00-15:00 solar time). Search domain per test, about 600 m for the equinox test. Energy precompute (Thermal-Sandbox pattern, Ladybug user-side only, pvlib candidate) stays optional.
recommendations.rationale: The guideline, not the teaching harness, governs a downtown block (adopted 17 Sep 2025 per Daily Hive, the dtmass README and a snippet of the PDF front matter; PDF unread). Our flat-ground arithmetic (NOAA formulas, 49.28 N, 123.12 W, 22 Sep 2026): 244-305 m towers cast about 470-590 m at 10:00 PDT, 450-560 m at 16:00 and 280-350 m near solar noon (about 13:05 PDT). So the 2.0-2.5 km solstice domain overstates the regulatory domain and dtmass's 320 m radius understates it. Not tested at tower scale; suncalc not cross-checked.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Solstice solar-time sun hours as the primary test; solar-time windows; Ladybug in-process (AGPL); copying the evaluator or dtmass code (no licence); a 320 m or 15 m search radius; encoding dtmass's park list or 1 m2 tolerance as fact.
